```{r}
#| label: setup
#| context: setup
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(plotly)
library(DT)
library(scales)
library(shiny)
library(leaflet)
library(bslib)
library(bsicons)
library(sf)

# ============================================================
# EPPS 6356
# Assignment 8 Dashboard + Assignment 9 Reactive Map
# Insang Lee
# ============================================================

dashboard_data <- read_csv(
  "subway_arrests_dashboard_2024.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(
    month = as.Date(month),
    borough_name = case_when(
      borough %in% c("M", "Manhattan") ~ "Manhattan",
      borough %in% c("Bk", "Brooklyn") ~ "Brooklyn",
      borough %in% c("Q", "Queens") ~ "Queens",
      borough %in% c("Bx", "Bronx") ~ "Bronx",
      borough %in% c("SI", "Staten Island") ~ "Staten Island",
      TRUE ~ borough
    )
  )

monthly_summary <- dashboard_data |>
  group_by(month) |>
  summarise(
    monthly_ridership = sum(monthly_ridership, na.rm = TRUE),
    arrest_count = sum(arrest_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    arrests_per_100k =
      arrest_count / monthly_ridership * 100000,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

station_summary <- dashboard_data |>
  group_by(
    station_complex,
    borough,
    borough_name
  ) |>
  summarise(
    total_ridership = sum(monthly_ridership, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_arrests = sum(arrest_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    arrests_per_100k =
      total_arrests / total_ridership * 100000,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

total_ridership <- sum(
  dashboard_data$monthly_ridership,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

total_arrests <- sum(
  dashboard_data$arrest_count,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

overall_rate <-
  total_arrests /
  total_ridership *
  100000

boroughs <- st_read(
  "nyc_boroughs.geojson",
  quiet = TRUE
) |>
  transmute(
    borough_name = boroname,
    geometry
  ) |>
  st_transform(4326)

borough_month <- dashboard_data |>
  group_by(
    month,
    borough_name
  ) |>
  summarise(
    monthly_ridership = sum(
      monthly_ridership,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    arrest_count = sum(
      arrest_count,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    arrests_per_100k =
      arrest_count /
      monthly_ridership *
      100000
  )

month_choices <- sort(
  unique(dashboard_data$month)
)
```

```{r}
#| context: server

output$overview_ridership <- renderPlotly({

  p <- ggplot(
    monthly_summary,
    aes(
      x = month,
      y = monthly_ridership,
      group = 1,
      text = paste0(
        "Month: ",
        format(month, "%B %Y"),
        "<br>Ridership: ",
        comma(monthly_ridership)
      )
    )
  ) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 2.5) +
    scale_x_date(
      date_breaks = "1 month",
      date_labels = "%b"
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = label_number(
        scale_cut = cut_short_scale()
      )
    ) +
    labs(
      x = "Month",
      y = "Monthly Ridership",
      caption = "Source: MTA Subway Hourly Ridership Data, 2024"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

  ggplotly(
    p,
    tooltip = "text"
  ) |>
    layout(
      hovermode = "x unified",
      xaxis = list(
        rangeslider = list(
          visible = TRUE
        )
      )
    )
})

output$overview_arrests <- renderPlotly({

  p <- ggplot(
    monthly_summary,
    aes(
      x = month,
      y = arrest_count,
      group = 1,
      text = paste0(
        "Month: ",
        format(month, "%B %Y"),
        "<br>Arrests: ",
        comma(arrest_count)
      )
    )
  ) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 2.5) +
    scale_x_date(
      date_breaks = "1 month",
      date_labels = "%b"
    ) +
    labs(
      x = "Month",
      y = "Number of Arrests",
      caption = "Source: NYPD Arrests Data, 2024; arrests within 500 meters of selected stations"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

  ggplotly(
    p,
    tooltip = "text"
  ) |>
    layout(
      hovermode = "x unified"
    )
})

map_data <- reactive({

  selected_month <- as.Date(
    input$map_month
  )

  d <- borough_month |>
    filter(
      month == selected_month
    )

  if (
    input$map_borough != "All"
  ) {
    d <- d |>
      filter(
        borough_name ==
          input$map_borough
      )
  }

  boroughs |>
    inner_join(
      d,
      by = "borough_name"
    )
})

station_map_data <- reactive({

  selected_month <- as.Date(
    input$map_month
  )

  d <- dashboard_data |>
    filter(
      month == selected_month
    ) |>
    group_by(
      station_complex,
      borough,
      borough_name
    ) |>
    summarise(
      monthly_ridership = sum(
        monthly_ridership,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      arrest_count = sum(
        arrest_count,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      arrests_per_100k =
        arrest_count /
        monthly_ridership *
        100000,
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  if (
    input$map_borough != "All"
  ) {
    d <- d |>
      filter(
        borough_name ==
          input$map_borough
      )
  }

  d
})

output$map_ridership <- renderText({

  comma(
    sum(
      map_data()$monthly_ridership,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )
})

output$map_arrests <- renderText({

  comma(
    sum(
      map_data()$arrest_count,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )
})

output$subway_map <- renderLeaflet({

  d <- map_data()

  req(
    nrow(d) > 0
  )

  pal <- colorNumeric(
    palette = "YlGnBu",
    domain = d$arrests_per_100k,
    na.color = "#d9d9d9"
  )

  leaflet(d) |>
    addTiles() |>
    addPolygons(
      fillColor = ~pal(arrests_per_100k),
      fillOpacity = 0.75,
      color = "white",
      weight = 1,
      label = ~paste0(
        borough_name,
        ": ",
        round(
          arrests_per_100k,
          2
        ),
        " arrests per 100,000 riders"
      ),
      popup = ~paste0(
        "<b>",
        borough_name,
        "</b>",
        "<br>Ridership: ",
        comma(
          monthly_ridership
        ),
        "<br>Arrests: ",
        comma(
          arrest_count
        ),
        "<br>Arrests per 100,000 riders: ",
        round(
          arrests_per_100k,
          2
        )
      )
    ) |>
    addLegend(
      pal = pal,
      values = ~arrests_per_100k,
      title = "Arrests per 100,000 riders",
      position = "bottomright"
    )
})

output$map_chart <- renderPlot({

  station_map_data() |>
    arrange(
      arrests_per_100k
    ) |>
    ggplot(
      aes(
        x = arrests_per_100k,
        y = fct_reorder(
          station_complex,
          arrests_per_100k
        )
      )
    ) +
    geom_col() +
    labs(
      x = "Arrests per 100,000 Riders",
      y = NULL,
      caption = "Sources: MTA Subway Hourly Ridership Data and NYPD Arrest Data"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
})

output$station_scatter <- renderPlotly({

  p <- ggplot(
    station_summary,
    aes(
      x = total_ridership,
      y = arrests_per_100k,
      color = borough,
      text = paste0(
        "Station: ",
        station_complex,
        "<br>Borough: ",
        borough,
        "<br>Total ridership: ",
        comma(total_ridership),
        "<br>Total arrests: ",
        comma(total_arrests),
        "<br>Arrests per 100,000 riders: ",
        round(
          arrests_per_100k,
          2
        )
      )
    )
  ) +
    geom_point(
      size = 4.5,
      alpha = 0.8
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      labels = label_number(
        scale_cut = cut_short_scale()
      )
    ) +
    labs(
      x = "Total Ridership, 2024",
      y = "Arrests per 100,000 Riders",
      color = "Borough",
      caption = "Sources: MTA Subway Hourly Ridership Data and NYPD Arrests Data, 2024"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )

  ggplotly(
    p,
    tooltip = "text"
  )
})

output$station_bubble <- renderPlotly({

  p <- ggplot(
    station_summary,
    aes(
      x = total_arrests,
      y = arrests_per_100k,
      size = total_ridership,
      color = borough,
      text = paste0(
        "Station: ",
        station_complex,
        "<br>Borough: ",
        borough,
        "<br>Total arrests: ",
        comma(total_arrests),
        "<br>Total ridership: ",
        comma(total_ridership),
        "<br>Arrests per 100,000 riders: ",
        round(
          arrests_per_100k,
          2
        )
      )
    )
  ) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.75) +
    scale_size_continuous(
      range = c(5, 18),
      labels = label_number(
        scale_cut = cut_short_scale()
      ),
      name = "2024 Ridership"
    ) +
    labs(
      x = "Total Arrests",
      y = "Arrests per 100,000 Riders",
      color = "Borough",
      caption = "Sources: MTA Subway Hourly Ridership Data and NYPD Arrests Data, 2024"
    ) +
    guides(
      color = guide_legend(
        title = "Borough"
      ),
      size = guide_legend(
        title = "2024 Ridership"
      )
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )

  ggplotly(
    p,
    tooltip = "text"
  )
})

output$station_table <- renderDT({

  station_summary |>
    arrange(
      desc(total_ridership)
    ) |>
    mutate(
      total_ridership =
        comma(total_ridership),
      total_arrests =
        comma(total_arrests),
      arrests_per_100k =
        round(
          arrests_per_100k,
          2
        )
    ) |>
    rename(
      Station = station_complex,
      Borough = borough,
      `Total Ridership` =
        total_ridership,
      `Total Arrests` =
        total_arrests,
      `Arrests per 100,000 Riders` =
        arrests_per_100k
    ) |>
    select(
      Station,
      Borough,
      `Total Ridership`,
      `Total Arrests`,
      `Arrests per 100,000 Riders`
    ) |>
    datatable(
      filter = "top",
      options = list(
        pageLength = 10,
        scrollX = TRUE
      ),
      rownames = FALSE
    )
})
```

# About

**Assignment 8 and Assignment 9 Dashboard: NYC Subway Ridership and Arrest Patterns**

This dashboard was initially created for **EPPS 6356 Assignment 8** and expanded for **Assignment 9** with a reactive spatial visualization.

The purpose of the dashboard is to examine subway ridership and arrest patterns across selected New York City subway stations while accounting for differences in passenger volume.

**Research Question**

How do subway ridership and arrest patterns vary across stations and over time, and how do patterns change after accounting for passenger volume?

**Data Sources**

- MTA Subway Hourly Ridership Data
- NYPD Arrest Data
- NYC Open Data Borough Boundaries

**Prototype Scope**

The dashboard uses **2024 data for nine selected high-ridership subway station complexes** in Manhattan, Queens, and Brooklyn.

The final project is planned to expand the analysis to the full subway network and the **2020–2024** period.

**Unit of Analysis**

**Station × month**

Monthly subway ridership and arrest measures are calculated for each selected station complex.

**Arrest Measure**

NYPD arrests were assigned to the **nearest selected subway station** when the arrest occurred within **500 meters** of that station.

This approach allows arrest activity near subway stations to be compared with passenger volume.

**Key Measures**

- Monthly subway ridership
- Monthly arrest count
- Arrests per 100,000 riders
- Station complex
- Borough
- Month

The ridership-adjusted arrest rate is calculated as:

**Arrests per 100,000 riders = (Monthly arrests / Monthly ridership) × 100,000**

**Visualizations**

The dashboard includes:

- Monthly time-series line charts
- Station-level scatter plot
- Ridership-adjusted bubble chart
- Reactive Leaflet choropleth map
- Reactive station-level comparison chart
- Interactive station-level data table

**Map Interaction**

Users can:

- Select a month
- Select a borough
- View updated ridership and arrest totals
- View ridership-adjusted arrest rates on the map
- Compare station-level arrest rates in the companion chart
- View borough information through map labels and popups

**AI Use Disclosure**

ChatGPT was used to assist with R coding, troubleshooting, and clarification of assignment requirements. I tested the suggested code in RStudio, reviewed the outputs, and made the final decisions about the dashboard design, data preparation, and content.
